_note: D2 (2026-10-31), see mesen2-results/D2_20261031.md. Vanilla engine facts measured on the SPC side: (1) FadeThenStartMusic's $01 after the $F1 echo does not stop the fade (the SPC already holds $08 = $01), so the fade is audible (master volume $53 to 0 over about 335 frames) and the thinker's $F0 follows the SPC's zero answer at fade end, not one or two frames after the $01. (2) $F2 = CmdF2 keys off all voices (KOFF $FF, volumes unchanged); $F0 = CmdStop (master and echo volume 0, FLG $20) and is not a 'ready signal'. (3) The resident loader writes no DSP register. Dry-run only: npm run merge -- plans/extracted-audit/mesen2-results/specs/D2_notes.json --dry-run. Comments go through expectOld because extracted/ carries no line-tracking tags; the apply pass may switch to expect after extract:lt. 'find' must occur exactly once in the stored note.

Measured: the $01 in step 2 has no effect while the engine's last-command byte ($08) already holds $01, so the fade started by $F1 runs to its end and is audible (master volume $53 to 0 in about 335 frames). The engine's fade-end code then calls CmdStop, which writes 0 to APUIO0; that zero is what step 2 waits for, so SpcTransferMusicData's $F0 follows the end of the fade, not one or two frames after the $01. While the main loop is blocked inside a dialogue wait the thinker does not run and the zero is read later.
